data.title: UBS hires Financial Advisors John Pham and Jimmy Yip in Silicon Valley
data.description:
UBS today announced that Financial Advisors John Pham and Jimmy Yip have joined the firm’s offices in Palo Alto and San Jose, California. The team joins UBS from Merrill Lynch and will be part of the UBS San Francisco Market, led by Market Executive Emily de la Reguera and reports to Silicon Valley Market Director Jacqueline Kehoe.

“We are thrilled to welcome John, Jimmy, and their team to UBS,” said Emily de la Reguera. “John and Jimmy have built an exceptional team grounded in thoughtful advice, deep relationships and an unwavering commitment to their clients. Their experience serving the unique needs of Silicon Valley executives, entrepreneurs and families, together with the strength of our global wealth management platform, makes them an outstanding addition to UBS and an important part of our continued growth in the region.”

Market Director Jacqueline Kehoe worked closely with this team during her tenure at Merrill Lynch. The strong relationships and trust she developed with the team were instrumental in their decision to join UBS. “I have had the opportunity to work alongside this team and witness firsthand their dedication to delivering outstanding client service and fostering long-term relationships,“ said Jacqueline.

John Pham brings more than 22 years of experience advising Silicon Valley executives, entrepreneurs and families. He is known for his thoughtful approach to wealth management and his commitment to building lasting client relationships. His practice is centered on understanding each client’s complete financial picture and developing personalized strategies aligned with their long-term goals.

Jimmy Yip brings extensive financial services experience and a goals-based approach to advising working professionals, business owners and their families. He focuses on understanding each client’s goals, concerns and aspirations and developing tailored investment and wealth management strategies. Jimmy has worked in the financial services industry since 2004 and earned a bachelor’s degree in business marketing from San Jose State University.

John and Jimmy are joined by Client Associates Leslie Vinoya, Kimberly Russell and Randall Bane, who bring deep experience and a shared commitment to delivering exceptional client service.

Notes to Editors

About UBS
UBS is a leading and truly global wealth manager and the leading universal bank in Switzerland. It also provides diversified asset management solutions and focused investment banking capabilities. UBS manages 7.3 trillion dollars of invested assets as per the second quarter 2026. UBS helps clients achieve their financial goals through personalized advice, solutions and products. Headquartered in Zurich, Switzerland, the firm is operating in more than 50 markets around the globe. UBS Group shares are listed on the SIX Swiss Exchange and the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE).

data.title: Nymex Overview: Crude Futures Fall on US-Iran Diplomacy, Supply Risks — OPIS
data.description:
Oil futures fell midday Friday amid renewed diplomatic efforts to reach a U.S.-Iran agreement over the Strait of Hormuz, while continued threats to the Middle East energy infrastructure kept supply concerns in focus.

As of 12:35 p.m. ET, November ICE Brent crude was trading $3.06 lower at $103.54, with December down $3.50 at $96.72/bbl. The November West Texas Intermediate contract was trading $2.63 lower at $91.98/bbl, with December down $2.80 at $88.10/bbl.

Refined product futures were also falling. October RBOB traded 18.5cts lower at $3.3796/gal, with November down 15.04cts at $3.1904/gal. The October ULSD contract traded 14.41cts lower at $4.5862/gal, with November down 9.66cts at $4.4314/gal.

Diplomatic efforts to reopen the Strait of Hormuz face obstacles. Qatar and other mediators are seeking a new round of talks in Oman as soon as next week, according to The Wall Street Journal, while Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates are urging Washington to maintain economic pressure on Iran and avoid concessions that would ease sanctions or the U.S. naval blockade.

The prospect of de-escalation is being weighed against continued threats to regional energy infrastructure. France plans to deploy soldiers, radar and defense systems to Saudi Arabia to help protect a refinery and crude-oil pipeline at the Red Sea port of Yanbu.

Near-term physical supply remains tight despite efforts to restore regional flows. Brent's front-month spread remained around $4 to $5/bbl, compared with less than $1/bbl in February, reflecting tight prompt supplies. The International Energy Agency said global observed oil inventories have fallen by 507 million bbl since the conflict began, including a 95 million-bbl draw in August.

Friday's decline follows a sharp rally Thursday, when Brent gained 3.4% and WTI rose 2.7% after Saudi Arabia reported intercepting missiles launched at the kingdom.

data.title: EU wheat eases again as Black Sea truce efforts assessed
data.description:
Euronext wheat fell on Friday to a one-month low as diplomatic initiatives raised hopes for a recovery in war-disrupted Black Sea exports, though continued attacks by Russia and Ukraine helped underpin prices, traders said.

Benchmark December milling wheat on Paris-based Euronext settled down 0.3% at €236.75 ($269.73) a metric ton after the day session.

The contract earlier dropped to €233.75, its lowest since August 25, with a chart gap created during an opening fall adding to selling momentum. But it later recovered to fill the gap and trade only slightly lower.

A slide in Chicago wheat , which fell around 3% before paring losses, pressured Euronext.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said on Friday the United States had proposed a trilateral meeting with Ukraine and Russia to discuss efforts to end the conflict, while the Kremlin said a trilateral meeting could happen soon.

Turkey, meanwhile, is pursuing efforts to broker a Black Sea truce.

Large long positions held by investors and careful buying by wheat importers have also encouraged the market off multi-year highs struck in early September.

"The market has been selling off with longs who are tired and consumers who will wait," a futures trader said.

Russia could quickly restart up to 80% of its grain terminal capacity in the Black Sea and Sea of Azov if diplomatic efforts result in a ceasefire, a Reuters analysis of industry data showed on Friday.

Continuing attacks by Russia and Ukraine, however, have tempered expectations of near-term de-escalation.

Grain markets also drew support from comments by US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer, who said Washington expected to release on Monday details on the outcome of trade negotiations with China.

That offset initial disappointment over the absence of news on agricultural trade during a US-China summit this week.

In France, a vessel is loading a first shipment of wheat for Yemen in years, LSEG data showed, as Black Sea disruption generates some unusual demand for French wheat.

French traders are watching to see if rain forecast for the week ahead materialises ahead of cereal planting and after record drought reduced rapeseed sowing.

($1 = 0.8777 euros)

data.title: NexTel Medical Corp. Showcases Pioneer Exosome Technologies and Diagnostic Innovations at Leading Healthcare Conference
data.description:
Company highlights ongoing clinical developments in traumatic brain injury (TBI) therapeutics and non-invasive cancer screening, sparking key vendor collaboration discussions.

ORLANDO, FL / ACCESS Newswire / September 25, 2026 / NexTel Medical Corp. (f/k/a Exousia Pro, Inc.) , a clinical-stage biotechnology company pioneering proprietary exosome-based delivery and diagnostic systems, today announced the successful participation of its executive and medical leadership teams at this week's Orlando Health Conference.

Throughout the event, NexTel executives and key scientific advisors engaged directly with industry founders, medical device distributors, and commercial sales representatives to present the company's expanding platform technologies.

Key scientific highlights from the conference include:

  • Scientific Presentations: Dr. Sugaya delivered a comprehensive, three-hour briefing detailing NexTel's core pipeline developments. Additionally, Dr. Hausman conducted a virtual presentation from California focused on Maxasome™ PLUS and its therapeutic applications for Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI). Dr. Hausman is currently preparing a white paper exploring the application of mushroom-derived exosomes in treating TBI.
  • Strategic Executive Presence: NexTel's Head of Operations and Chief Executive Officer represented the company on-site throughout the week to drive high-level business development and strategic networking.
  • Commercialization & Educational Initiatives: Based on feedback gathered from market representatives, NexTel is updating its clinical and consumer educational materials to streamline product messaging. The company is actively producing a series of video tutorials demonstrating how its liquid biopsy cancer screening platform detects early-stage biomarkers in saliva, alongside educational modules outlining the therapeutic scope of Maxasome™ PLUS.

"Our strong presence at this week's conference underscored the immense market potential for our exosome delivery and diagnostic platforms," said Mathew Dwyer, Chief Executive Officer of NexTel Medical Corp. "The overwhelming interest from industry partners reinforces our confidence in our technology pipeline. We are already scheduling follow-up discussions regarding strategic vendor collaborations, while actively refining our educational outreach to accelerate clinical adoption."

As a result of the enthusiastic reception from industry stakeholders, NexTel leadership is scheduled to conduct follow-up commercialization and partnership discussions with several prominent vendors next week.

About NexTel Medical Corp.

NexTel Medical Corp. is a pioneering biotechnology leader at the forefront of exosome research, clinical diagnostics, and wellness accessibility. The Company specializes in developing proprietary, next-generation, exosome-based delivery systems and non-invasive screening tools designed to revolutionize both therapeutic and diagnostic modalities.

NexTel's fully integrated ecosystem spans four core strategic divisions, bridging the gap between complex biotech innovation and scalable market delivery:

data.title: Buyback plans are slowing but 2026 may still be a record
data.description:
Key points:
  • Main US indexes advance; Dow out front, up ~0.8%
  • Tech leads S&P 500 sector gainers; energy is weakest group
  • Dollar, bitcoin dip; US crude down >2.5%; gold up slightly
  • US 10-year Treasury yield rises to ~5.20%

BUYBACK PLANS ARE SLOWING BUT 2026 MAY STILL BE A RECORD

In a choppy year for share buybacks, EPFR is reporting "exceptionally light" announcements so far in September.

After announcements of buyback authorizations adding up to $973.7 billion in the first six months of the year, EPFR analyst Winston Chua notes that momentum has "reversed sharply" since mid-year.

From July through September 23, buyback announcements of $196.4 billion compared with $368.5 billion in the same timeframe a year ago, marking a decline of roughly 50%.

And with just a week left in September at the time of his tally, announcements had totaled $20 billion compared with the $67 billion total for September in 2025 and the 10-year September average of $61.5 billion, according to the data from EPFR, a unit of ISI Markets.

The slowdown comes after the $133.8 billion announced in August and $42.8 billion in July.

"If this month’s figures fall below $25 billion, it will mark the second-lowest September volume in 15 years," according to Chua, but he wrote that the slowdown appeared to reflect "a lack of large programs rather than a broad-based retreat from buybacks."

But even with the recent slowdown, he wrote that a strong first half of 2026 means that a full-year record is still within reach.

"Roughly $250 billion of additional announcements would still surpass 2025’s $1.39 trillion total," he wrote, noting that in the last five years fourth-quarter buybacks averaged $271 billion.

data.title: Sustainability becomes a business
data.description:
The Sustainable Hospitality Conversations, titled ‘Sustainability That Pays: Turning Responsible Hospitality into Business Advantage’, brought together industry leaders to discuss how responsible practices can support both environmental goals and commercial outcomes

With the conversations of Day 1 setting the tone for what lies ahead, the BW Hotelier Indian Hospitality Summit & Awards (IHA 2026) returned for its second day at the JW Marriott New Delhi Aerocity. The opening day brought together hospitality leaders, developers, investors, global brands and industry veterans, with discussions spanning growth, capital, development, leadership and the changing business of hospitality. Day 2 picked up from where those conversations left off, bringing a fresh set of voices and perspectives to the table.

As sustainability becomes increasingly linked to operational efficiency, cost management and long-term business performance, the hospitality sector is looking beyond compliance to identify tangible business value. The Sustainable Hospitality Conversations, titled ‘Sustainability That Pays: Turning Responsible Hospitality into Business Advantage’, brought together industry leaders to discuss how responsible practices can support both environmental goals and commercial outcomes.

The discussion was chaired by Dr Nitin Shankar Nagrale, Founder & General Secretary, HPMF [CEO India and Emerging Markets, Quality NZ Imports Pvt Ltd] and brought together Sireesha Chandana, VP Learning & Development and Sustainability, Indian Hotels Company Limited (IHCL); Akanksha Singh, Global Senior Manager - Sustainability, Radisson Hotel Group; and Priyanka Rajgadkar Gilhotra, Associate Vice President – ESG, Leela Palaces, Hotels & Resorts Limited, Srinivasan Mani, All India Head Sales & Marketing -Scroll & Screw Chillers, Blue Star and Nihan Sevnic, Marketing Communications, Emerging Markets, Diversey

Nagrale said, “Over the last two days, we spoke about growth, finance, people, technology and operations, but there is another important issue we need to address — sustainability and how we make growth sustainable, not merely environmentally but economically. Many times, we think sustainability is an alien concept or somebody else’s job, and organisations have created dedicated ESG or sustainability departments to address it. Today, we need to understand how sustainability can also become more economical. Owners often have the impression that following sustainability makes operations more expensive, but with daily consumption of energy, water, food, supplies and linen, the question is how we can make the asset life more economical and stretch it for decades.”

Chandana explained, “Sustainability happened to me by default, but in hindsight, after four years, I can say this is one of the best decisions we took. Sustainability has multiple aspects, with environmental stewardship being one of the largest, but there is also a significant aspect associated with human capital within the organisation and the community.

It cannot be managed by one person or a small team; it requires the entire organisation to put its mind behind it. To me, sustainability has to become part of the culture of the organisation, much like customer obsession. Every stakeholder, from our employees and value-chain partners to vendors and owner partners, is part of making sustainability happen every single day. Today’s youth are also looking for roles that give them purpose and passion, and they get that opportunity when they join an organisation that puts sustainability at the centre of what it does.”

Singh said, “Scaling up sustainability is not about sharing the same sustainability list with all hotels. We work with different owners, geographies, policies and resources, so we set the starting point and the finishing point, but allow each hotel to take its own route. The conversation with owners has also shifted from environmental practices and benefits for the planet to how we make the business more profitable if it is sustainable. The language owners want to hear is GOP, risk, asset value and ROI. The solution can be different for every hotel, but the ambition is the same — achieving sustainability without showing a loss in the P&L. The sustainability professional also needs to understand the business before talking about the planet.”

Sevnic explained, “As a trusted partner at Diversey, our role is to solve sustainability and operational challenges for our partners. We embed sustainability in everything we do — every innovation, operation, system and partnership. The best result does not come from chemistry alone; it is a combination of the right and safer formulation, precise dosing, efficient equipment, standard procedures, trained employees and reliable data.

Every rewash and repeat clean wastes water, energy, chemicals and employee time. Water must also be treated as a strategic resource, with hotels understanding where every litre is used. IoT-enabled platforms can provide visibility and track water, energy and chemical use in real time, while super-concentrated products and closed-loop dosing can reduce plastic, packaging, CO2, transport and storage.”

Rajgadkar said, “Hospitality is quite a complex problem to be solved because behind the small experience we give, and when we say The Leela is a truly Indian luxury brand, we want to focus all our energies on giving that Indian luxury experience to the guest. Every initiative has a story behind the experience we create. Whether it is Leela Ke Phool, where around nine metric tonnes of floral waste have been upcycled over the last three years, or Tishya fragrance, where the bottles use recycled plastic material, sustainability is embedded in what we do. Sustainability also has a direct connection with operating costs, because costs can be reduced when fuel and power consumption are reduced. We currently have 20.25 MW of installed solar and wind capacity across our hotels, and our fuel cost as a percentage of revenue has moved from 3.9 per cent to almost or below 3 per cent.”

Mani said, “When it comes to cooling, there are multiple options available, and there is no one solution that fits all. Every property is unique, so we look at each property individually and consider the total life-cycle cost instead of focussing only on the Capex. That is the approach we take at Blue Star when developing cooling solutions.”

Ultimately, the session highlighted a pivotal shift in how the hospitality sector views sustainability—transitioning from compliance to a strategic business imperative. The insights shared by operational and procurement leaders demonstrated that responsible practices, when executed across engineering and supply networks, serve as a dual driver for financial growth and long-term brand equity across the industry.

The conversations will eventually give way to celebration as IHA 2026 heads into its Gala Awards evening. Bringing the two-day gathering to its culmination, BW Hotelier will recognise accomplished hoteliers and hospitality organisations across 20+ categories, acknowledging the people and businesses that have contributed to the sector’s growth and evolution.

data.title: Trust and reputation take centre stage in hospitality branding
data.description:
The Brand & Reputation Conversations, titled ‘Building Brands Guests Believe In: Trust, Reputation & the New Hospitality Advantage’, brought together senior commercial, brand and communications leaders to discuss the role of credibility and reputation in shaping hospitality brands

With the conversations of Day 1 setting the tone for what lies ahead, the BW Hotelier Indian Hospitality Summit & Awards (IHA 2026) returned for its second day at the JW Marriott New Delhi Aerocity. The opening day brought together hospitality leaders, developers, investors, global brands and industry veterans, with discussions spanning growth, capital, development, leadership and the changing business of hospitality. Day 2 picked up from where those conversations left off, bringing a fresh set of voices and perspectives to the table.

As hospitality brands navigate a more discerning and connected guest landscape, trust and reputation are becoming increasingly important to how brands build lasting relationships with consumers. The Brand & Reputation Conversations, titled ‘Building Brands Guests Believe In: Trust, Reputation & the New Hospitality Advantage’, brought together senior commercial, brand and communications leaders to discuss the role of credibility and reputation in shaping hospitality brands.

The discussion was chaired by Saurabh Rai, Executive Vice President, Preferred Hotels and Resorts, and brought together Parveen Chander Kumar, EVP, Commercials, IHCL; Manish Tolani, VP & Commercial Dir, Hilton South Asia; Kadambini Mittal, Regional VP Commercial India & South Asia, Hyatt; Sarah Walker-Kerr, Head of Corporate Affairs IMEA, InterContinental Hotels & Resorts (IHG), Dubai; Anjali Mehra, Executive Vice President – Brand & Communications, The Leela Palaces Hotels and Resorts; and Vaibhav Jain, Sr VP Sales, Lemon Tree Hotels.

Rai said, “There has been no time in the history of our industry when we have thrown more resources, more money, more passion and more love into building more brands, more collections and more sub-collections. With the growth spurt that we are experiencing in India and pretty much around the world, the industry is seeing an unprecedented focus on creating more brands and collections. Truth be told, while we are busy doing all of this, the question is whether the customer really cares.”

Kumar said, “Today, there are different price points and different cohorts being formed, and technology is playing an important role in how consumers are segmented through the digital footprints they leave behind. People do care about brands; what is really important is that the brand needs to be differentiated. We don’t want everything to be called Taj. We want different kinds of brands which stand for different things and cater to different needs for travel at different stages.”

Tolani said, “Sometimes it is critically important to understand whether our brands are earning their space on the shelf and whether they are as differentiated to customers as they are to us. If all things are kept similar, the key differentiator is the brand voice and brand promise, and whether you have delivered on that promise. The second is whether you are making the dreaming, booking and staying journey frictionless. I would pay more for convenience and for somebody who understands what I am trying to say. The third is loyalty beyond points. We need to look at loyalty as an ecosystem of partnerships that gives consumers more reasons to keep coming back. Ultimately, all of this boils down to conversion, revenue, owner economics and returns.”

Mittal addressed, “We have 36 brands, and what has changed is that we have become a brand-led and insight-focused organisation. When customers are travelling, the occasions are different, so the important part is what you provide for those different occasions. For us, the common thread is care. Care is about how you connect with the guest and how you build trust with them.

That trust drives preference, and once preference is there, how are you creating long-term value? The purpose of travel can be different, whether it is business travel, travelling with friends or being a solo traveller, but care, preference, trust and long-term value are what help us build an emotional connect with the customer, differentiate and drive a higher price point.”

Walker-Kerr said, “Corporate affairs is a very, very serious function, particularly when India is going through such massive growth. We have to make sure the business is doing the right thing all the time. That is where people like myself come in, making sure we are engaged across the owner community, engaging with the government and through industry advocacy. We are also helping to control that conversation so that we can get the business right as well. So, it is a very hard-nosed and very serious function.”

Mehra, “For me, the story of India’s growth is not necessarily about scale. I think it is about meaning, resonance, relevance and how you are making a difference in the life of that end consumer. We have chosen to be a pure-play luxury brand, and we believe that more brands do not necessarily mean more choice. What is important is who you are as a brand, who you want to be to whom and how you bring that to life.

All the touchpoints that you create need to tell that story across every guest journey. At Alila, we have tried to do that through our sonic identity, signature fragrance, palace services and ceremonial rituals. These golden threads create differentiation and meaning. We are not trying to give customers more choice, but more reasons to choose us over some of the other choices they have.”

Jain said, “I don’t think AI is ever going to do the controlling. The controlling has always remained in the hands of the consumer. You need to integrate with the new technology, but the fundamental storytelling is something that will remain in the hands of consumers. One must also understand that the brand is influenced by all stakeholders. Brand building and consciousness about what the brand is should be broader than what the consumer gets.”

Wrapping up the session, panellists highlighted that building brand preference today requires far more than polished marketing campaigns. By aligning core brand values with flawless operational delivery, leading hotel groups across India are fostering true brand loyalty and securing sustainable commercial growth in a fierce marketplace.

The conversations will eventually give way to celebration as IHA 2026 heads into its Gala Awards evening. Bringing the two-day gathering to its culmination, BW Hotelier will recognise accomplished hoteliers and hospitality organisations across 20+ categories, acknowledging the people and businesses that have contributed to the sector’s growth and evolution.

data.title: FSLR Stock Heads For Its Worst Week In Over A Month — Roth Says US Polysilicon Crackdown Could Provide A Tailwind
data.description:
Key points:
  • Roth called current FSLR levels a “very attractive entry point” despite concerns over weaker-than-expected solar-module pricing.
  • The firm also sees T1 Energy and Toyo as potential beneficiaries.
  • New U.S. rules target polysilicon stockpiling, with Roth saying more than 20 importer licenses have already been revoked.

First Solar (FSLR) was on investors’ radar on Friday after Roth Capital said a crackdown on polysilicon stockpiling could tighten supplies and support higher pricing for domestic solar manufacturers.

The call comes after FSLR shares tumbled nearly 11% on Thursday and headed for their biggest weekly loss in six weeks. Roth attributed the selloff to concerns that solar-module pricing may not be as strong as previously expected.

However, the brokerage sees the recent weakness as a buying opportunity, calling current levels a “very attractive entry point.”

At the time of writing, FSLR stock was up 3.5%

Roth Says FLSR Could Benefit From Supply Tailwinds

Earlier this week, the Commerce Department’s Bureau of Industry and Security implemented a temporary rule to prevent companies from stockpiling polysilicon and related products before new Section 232 import measures take effect on December 4. The rule allows the government to restrict companies that import significantly more polysilicon than their historical levels, while new importers are subject to weekly limits.

The move follows President Donald Trump’s August proclamation imposing minimum import prices on polysilicon, wafers, solar cells, and modules, as well as a 15% tariff on covered polysilicon derivatives beginning in December.

Roth said its channel checks showed imports had increased more than expected and that it learned more than 20 importer licenses had already been revoked. The firm expects stricter enforcement to reduce stockpiling, restrict supply and ultimately support higher U.S. pricing.

The firm sees First Solar, T1 Energy (TE) and Toyo (TOYO) as potential beneficiaries.

FSLR’s Mixed Q2

First Solar reported a mixed second quarter. While revenue fell 4% to $1.06 billion, partly due to customer contract terminations, earnings rose 23% to $3.92 per share.

The company also maintained its full-year outlook, forecasting $4.9 billion to $5.2 billion in sales and adjusted earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortization (EBITDA) of $2.6 billion to $2.8 billion. The company ended June with a contracted backlog of 45.1 GW extending through 2030.

data.title: Gasoline refining margins end week lower
data.description:
Northwest European gasoline refining margins dropped 92 cents to $45.01 a barrel on Friday, marking a roughly $2 drop from last Friday's level.

data.title: Subway, soccer and spats: New York's Mamdani a UN week attraction
data.description:
Key points:
  • Mayor becomes an unexpected draw during UN week
  • Trump praises Mamdani despite political differences
  • Netanyahu turns mayor into target in UN address

By Michelle Nichols

The United Nations wasn't the only New York attraction for visiting world leaders this week – Mayor Zohran Mamdani emerged as a popular draw for like-minded politicians and a target for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

The 34-year-old former state lawmaker, who took office on January 1 in New York City, rode the subway with Ireland's Prime Minister Micheal Martin, exchanged soccer jerseys with Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, and talked to students with Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store about artificial intelligence.

"In a year when the main sentiment around the UN is existential gloom about the state of the world, a perky young politico was what we all needed," said Richard Gowan, director of global issues and institutions at the International Crisis Group.

"Of course a meeting with Mamdani is pretty politically low-risk for most leaders. You spend some time on the subway and with school kids. Nobody is going to ask you to solve the North Korea nuclear problem," he added.

The New York mayor was also a focus of Netanyahu's Thursday address to the 193-member UN General Assembly in which he berated Mamdani for calling him a war criminal over Israel's actions in Gaza.

Mamdani discussed "Building an Economy for the Many” over breakfast with Spain's President Pedro Sánchez, Barbados Prime Minister Mia Mottley and European Council President António Costa, and met LGBTQ+ youth with Dutch Prime Minister Rob Jetten.

Costa, a former mayor of Lisbon, told Mamdani at the event on Tuesday: "You have the best job that a politician can do – I miss the ability mayors sometimes have of identifying a problem in the morning and having it solved by the end of the day."

Austrian President Alexander Van der Bellen and British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband also had meetings with Mamdani.

WAR OF WORDS WITH NETANYAHU

While Democrat Mamdani's meetings were largely with world leaders of similar political leanings, there was one notable exception: Republican US President Donald Trump.

As Trump's ally Netanyahu escalated a war of words with New York's first Muslim mayor, Trump met with Mamdani at Gracie Mansion, the mayor's official residence.

"I want him to be a great mayor, and he's certainly got potential, got great potential," Trump said at a joint press conference with Mamdani after their meeting on Monday.

Netanyahu's address on Thursday was a stark contrast.

"You tried to stop me from coming here. You tried. You tried to silence me. Well, you can't silence me. You can't silence the truth," Netanyahu, Israel's longest-serving leader, said of Mamdani.

Mamdani campaigned for office on a promise to have Netanyahu arrested for alleged war crimes should he visit the largest US city, but later said he determined he lacked the legal authority to do so. This week, Mamdani described Netanyahu as "the architect of a horrific genocide against Palestinians."

The evening before Netanyahu's arrival, Mamdani posted a video on social media of him planting an olive tree at Gracie Mansion with Palestinian families from Gaza with the caption: "May peace be our future."

Making his first visit to New York on Thursday since Mamdani took office, Netanyahu told the General Assembly: "Israel didn't commit genocide. Israel prevented genocide."

In response, Mamdani accused Netanyahu of using his UN speech "to repeat baseless lies meant to sanitize his genocide of Palestinians," adding: "Yet no lie can change the fact that he remains the subject of an International Criminal Court arrest warrant alleging war crimes and crimes against humanity.”

Israel rejects genocide allegations and says its military campaign targets Hamas, not Gaza’s civilian population. It says it takes steps to minimize civilian harm and says Hamas fighters embed among civilians.

data.title: Correction to U.S. Appeals Court Upholds Pentagon Labeling Anthropic a Security Risk Article — WSJ
data.description:
By Amrith Ramkumar and Heather Somerville

WASHINGTON-A federal appeals court upheld the Defense Department's decision to designate Anthropic a security risk, giving the Trump administration a win in its complicated feud with one of the nation's top artificial-intelligence developers.

The federal appeals court in Washington said in a 2-1 decision Friday that the law giving the Pentagon the authority to deem a company a supply-chain risk gave Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth the latitude to take the action against Anthropic because the company's refusal to have its AI tools used in mass surveillance or autonomous weapons could undermine military operations.

"The Department had ample support for its conclusion that the continued integration of Claude into the Department's information systems, by the Department or its contractors, presented a statutorily covered national-security risk," the court wrote. Anthropic had argued that the designation was an unprecedented attack retaliating against the company for disagreeing with the Defense Department in contract negotiations. A federal judge in California recently sided with the company in a parallel dispute covering parts of the designation under a different statute, fueling uncertainty about the future of the supply-chain risk label.

Legal analysts have said that a split between the courts could ultimately lead to the Supreme Court.

"We respectfully disagree with the court's decision. Another federal court has already held the government's parallel designation unlawful. We remain confident in our position and are considering all options, including further review," an Anthropic spokeswoman said.

The supply-chain risk is normally used on companies based in foreign adversaries like China's Huawei who pose security risks. AI analysts have said the administration's move was a self-inflicted wound in the global AI race because it could damage Anthropic, which makes some of the nation's most powerful models and has said it has lost contracts and suffered reputational harm from the move.

A win for the government could give the Pentagon more latitude to take similar actions against companies in the future, analysts have said.

The rulings are part of a delicate relationship between the Trump administration and Anthropic, which are working together on the release of new AI models while the legal fight continues. The company has vaulted ahead in the AI race by many measures and is barreling toward an initial public offering in which it is aiming for a valuation of about $2 trillion.

Pentagon officials have said the department is nearly entirely done moving away from Anthropic's models using tools from OpenAI and other competitors.

At a hearing at the federal appeals court earlier this year, the three-judge panel appeared split, with two of the judges seeming sympathetic to the administration's argument that it had the authority to use the supply-chain risk designation regardless of the guardrails Anthropic was pursuing in their negotiations.

"It's about risk, and they say, 'Well, based on what we know, we can't trust that the [AI] model may not have something embedded within it that is going to create a problem for military capabilities," said Neomi Rao, a judge appointed during the first Trump administration.

Judge Karen LeCraft Henderson, who was appointed by former President George H.W. Bush, disagreed and published a dissenting opinion Thursday. "To me this is just a spectacular overreach by the department," she said during the hearing.

Write to Amrith Ramkumar at amrith.ramkumar@wsj.com and Heather Somerville at heather.somerville@wsj.com

data.title: Some Cruise Operators Are Covertly Offering Lower Fares — Market Talk
data.description: Many cruise lines have been offering covert fares--or fares that can only be offered by phone when someone calls to book, and cannot be offered on a website--to select sellers, UBS analysts say, citing a recent conversation with a large cruise seller. The covert fares are largely being offered for last-minute European bookings, as well as upcoming trips to the Caribbean and Bahamas, the analysts say in a research note. "Covert fares are typically a sign that cruise lines don't want to disrupt bookings that are already in hand by having lower rates available in the market," the analysts say. "And interestingly, these covert fares were only being offered to the largest 5-6 sellers, not to most sellers." (connor.hart@wsj.com)

data.title: US energy firms add rigs for third week in a row, says Baker Hughes
data.description:
By Scott DiSavino

U.S. energy firms this week added rigs for a third week in a row for the first time since July, energy services firm Baker Hughes said in its closely followed report on Friday.

The total oil and gas rig count, an early indicator of future output, rose by four to 599 in the week to September 25, its highest since May 2024. (BHGUSWTT), (BHGUSOILDRLW), (BHGUSGASDRLW) (USOIRC=ECI), (USGSRC=ECI)

Baker Hughes said this week's increase puts the total rig count up 50 rigs, or 9% above this time last year.

Baker Hughes said oil rigs rose by three to 455 this week, their highest since mid-August. It said gas rigs rose by one to 135, their highest since July 2023, and other miscellaneous rigs held at nine.

The oil and gas rig count declined by 7% in 2025, 5% in 2024, and 20% in 2023 as lower U.S. oil prices prompted energy firms to focus more on boosting shareholder returns and paying down debt rather than increasing output.

Since crude prices have surged during the US-Israeli war on Iran, the U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA) projected that crude output will rise from a record 13.7 million barrels per day (bpd) in 2025 to 13.8 million bpd in 2026.

On the gas side, EIA projected output will jump from a record 107.6 billion cubic feet per day (bcfd) in 2025 to 111.7 bcfd in 2026 as demand for the fuel rises to produce electricity for power-hungry data centers and liquefied natural gas (LNG) for export.

data.title: The Cheapest Stocks in the S&P 500: Are They a Bargain or a Trap? — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Jack Hough

Inflation is stubbornly high, but not in home broadband service. There, telecom operators are making fiberoptic inroads in a business long dominated by cable television companies. The result has been discounting: UBS reports that prices for various broadband service tiers are down 7% to 14% for fiber over the past year, and 17% to 27% for cable.

For telecom, this is a good deal. Wireless customers will hop from one carrier to another to score lower monthly bills or free phones, but they rarely change, or even think about, the main internet connection coming into their homes. By bundling the two together at a discount, telecoms can hold down churn in their wireless accounts, much the way cable has long done with broadband and pay television. For cable, however, this telecom insurgency looks like a second death. First, streaming companies came for pay TV. Now, telecoms are taking share in broadband.

The first death wasn't so painful. In late 2015, when Walt Disney disclosed that ESPN subscriptions had fallen by seven million over two years, investors made up their minds. Streaming wasn't just a way for studios to pick up extra money licensing their catalogs to Netflix and others; it was an existential threat to the cable TV bundle. Shares of networks and cable carriers tumbled for weeks. But cable had a backup plan: raise stand-alone broadband prices for customers who "cut the cord" on cable TV.

Cable TV amounts to reselling programming. After cable companies pay studios carriage fees for their cable networks, and retransmission fees for their local broadcasts, gross profit margins are left at 30% to 40%. With broadband, once the lines are installed, costs to add new customers are minimal, and gross margins can reach 70% to 90%. Cable companies faced with losing a $120 a month TV-plus-internet customer could simply raise the cost of internet service from $50 inside the bundle to $80 as a stand-alone.

The Covid-19 pandemic made fast home internet service a must, and cable companies added millions of new customers and raised prices. Share prices for Comcast and Charter Communications peaked in 2021. Telecom companies at the time were spending massive sums to build out their 5G service networks. But by 2023, with the move to 5G largely paid for, telecom spending fell and cash flow swelled. The obvious choice for putting these funds to work was laying more fiber, both for cellular backhaul, which offloads data traffic and makes networks faster, and home internet connections.

The result has been unpleasant for cable shareholders. Comcast-which spun off its cable networks and digital ventures such as Versant early this year and still has the NBC broadcast network, Peacock streaming, and Universal studios and theme parks-has lost nearly 60% in stock market value over the past five years. Charter, a cable pure play, has lost 84%.

Deep-value investors might be tempted. Charter now goes for just three times forward earnings projections, the lowest in the S&P 500, and Comcast sells for six times earnings, the sixth-lowest. But the outlook is daunting. Fiber broadband, which is generally superior to cable on speed and stability, still has only about a 22% market share, compared with 56% for cable. But fiber availability has expanded to 65% of households, and is expected to top 90% by 2030, spurring further fiber share gains.

Two lesser competitors loom, too. Fixed wireless service, whereby telecoms use spare cellular spectrum to offer home internet connections, is no match for fiber on speed but has nonetheless grabbed a quick 14% share of broadband thanks to aggressive telecom bundling. And Starlink satellite service, with a 4% share, is pricey but is cutting into cable in rural markets.

For cable, the best defense might be an upgrade path called Docsis 4.0, which allows for fiberlike speeds on existing copper wires. Since cable was built for television-a downloaded service-its upload speeds are slow. Docsis 4.0 can achieve the upload/download symmetry of fiber with speeds that are good enough for most users. To retain customers in the meantime, cable operators are offering cut-rate mobile phone service, using connections bought from Verizon and others, and bundling streaming services with broadband.

For Comcast in particular, the Versant spinoff this year was supposed to quarantine the most challenged part of the business-cable networks-and leave behind a core of healthy growers. The question now is whether its broadband business is weak enough to warrant spinning off, too. Investors might want to hold off on cable altogether. UBS says the best pick among cable and telecom companies is AT&T. It started later than Verizon in fiber broadband but has far surpassed it in availability, including through the acquisition earlier this year of the fiber business of Lumen Technologies, which provides plenty of room for bundling and growth.

Let's end with a quick word on fitness, banking, and robot revenge. Earlier this month, Barron's highlighted eight stocks that can grow without much help from artificial intelligence. Among them was a catch-the-falling-knife pick, Planet Fitness, already down more than 50% this year on disappointing sign-ups. It fell more this past week on fears that Muse, a new personal AI assistant from Meta Platforms, takes the effort out of canceling memberships that consumers had forgotten about. Another pick, Charles Schwab, is off to a weak start, too, amid concern that Muse will nudge its customers to move their low-interest deposits into something that pays better.

Wall Street is still trying to get a handle on the extent of its Muse risk. When Life Time, a chain of posh gyms, fell along with Planet Fitness, the analyst at Jefferies, who likes both stocks, pointed out that while Planet Fitness members pay as little as $10 to $15 a month, Life Time members pay $245. "Nobody forgets this bill," he wrote.

Write to Jack Hough at jack.hough@barrons.com and subscribe to his Barron's Streetwise podcast.

data.title: Minister MB Patil holds talks with Gan Siow Huang, Singapore Minister of State for Trade and Industry
data.description:
Bengaluru, Sept. 25 -- CapitaLand Investment, a global real asset manager, is keen to expand its data centre capacity in Karnataka, in addition to the 42 MW data centre it is developing at International Tech Park Bangalore in Bengaluru, with an investment of approximately Rs 2,000 crore, Karnataka Minister for Large and Medium Industries MB Patil, who is visiting Singapore to attract investments to the State, said on Friday.

In a media release following discussions with several companies, Patil said ST Telemedia Global Data Centres (STT GDC), a leading data centre platform with a significant presence in India, has expressed interest in further expanding its data centre presence in the State. STT GDC operates 34 data centres across 10 cities with more than 613 MW of IT capacity, including three facilities in Bengaluru. The company is investing approximately Rs 5,000 crore to develop a 100 MW data centre campus on KIADB land in Devanahalli, he said.

Patil said there was considerable scope for deeper Karnataka-Singapore collaboration across high-value sectors such as aerospace and defence, semiconductors, aviation MRO and other advanced industries. These opportunities were discussed with Gan Siow Huang, Minister of State for Trade and Industry, Singapore.

He said further progress in this regard would be pursued through Invest Karnataka Forum and the Singapore Enterprise Centre in Bengaluru. The Singapore Government has also been invited to participate as a partner country at the Global Investor Meet 2027 to be held next year, he added.

Patil stated that the Government of Karnataka encouraged TVS Motor Company, which already has a manufacturing presence in the State, to increase investments in manufacturing, electric mobility, advanced automotive technologies, and research and development.

Hardik Gesota, Managing Director and Head, India Private Funds, CapitaLand Investment; Rohith Bhandary, Head, Investments, CapitaLand India Trust; Ritu Mehlawat, Head of Investment, India, and Eugene Lim, Senior Investment Manager, India, of ST Telemedia Global Data Centres; and Sudarshan Venu, Chairman and Managing Director, TVS Motor Company, participated in the discussions.

Industries Department Principal Secretary Selvakumar and other officials were part of the Karnataka Government delegation.

data.title: Las Vegas looks to boost traffic with rare resort-wide sale
data.description:
Las Vegas is on the tail end of a rare citywide five-day sale that ran this week. The Vegas 5-Day sale sees resorts cut prices on rooms, dining, entertainment, and attractions as the industry looks to boost tourism amid an uneven recovery period.

The Vegas 5-Day Sale, running from September 22 through September 26, features more than 180 offers across the Strip, downtown, and surrounding resort corridors. Participating properties are advertising discounts of up to 60% on hotel stays, while other promotions include restaurant credits, show tickets, spa services, attractions, and multi-night packages.

The event is unusual because the offers are coordinated across the destination and compressed into a five-day booking window. The Las Vegas Convention and Visitors Authority launched the first such citywide sale in September 2025, calling it the "Fabulous 5-Day Sale." This year’s event is only its second iteration and expanded to more than 180 deals.

The gambling and entertainment city drew about 38.5M visitors in 2025, a 7.5% decline from the prior year and roughly 3.1M fewer people than in 2024. However, through July this year, visitation had edged 0.5% higher year over year, with July alone up 2.7%, suggesting a modest rebound is gearing up. International travel remains a concern as Canadian visitation, historically the city’s largest international source, remains about 30% below 2019 levels.

data.title: Bitget clarifies $388M in assets affected by security breach
data.description:
Crypto exchange Bitget released an updated incident report on Thursday’s security breach, clarifying that about $388 million in assets had been affected and not $352 million as previously reported.

In a Friday update, Bitget said it would continue to pause withdrawals following the security breach, and the company had launched a bounty program to incentivize freezing or recovering the assets. The exchange confirmed that “$387.5 million were transferred to attacker-controlled addresses” based on onchain tracing — about $35 million more than reported on Thursday.

“The revised figure reflects a more complete accounting of transfers that occurred during the incident, adding affected assets on Zcash and TRON that were not included in the initial estimate,” said Bitget. “It does not reflect further unauthorized transfers. The incident remains contained and no further unauthorized transfers are possible.”

According to Bitget, the incident included addresses on Ethereum Virtual Machine (EVM) networks, the XRP Ledger, Zcash and TRON. Among the assets stolen were XRP, Ether (ETH), Tether’s USDt (USDT), Zcash (ZEC), USDC, USDT0, XAUt, BNB, AVAX and TRX. The follow-up report did not address comments made by CEO Gracy Chen on Thursday speculating that a North Korean hacking group may have been behind the attack.

Even with the update on the assets transferred to hacker-controlled addresses, the Bitget security breach remains one of the largest to impact the industry. Hackers stole about $1.5 billion worth of Ether from Bybit in February 2025.

This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260925045354/en/

Alpha Fire Company is an all-volunteer department that responds to a wide range of emergencies beyond fires, including fire prevention and traffic safety at emergencies. Protecting approximately 130,000 people across State College Borough, College Township, Ferguson Township, Patton Township, and the Penn State University campus, it is the third-largest fire department in Pennsylvania by population served.

"For more than a century, Alpha Fire Company has been a trusted presence in the State College community, serving neighbors during emergencies and helping keep people safe every day," said Natalie Sunderland, Chief Marketing Officer at Bloom Energy. We also thank State Representatives Scott Conklin and Paul Takac for joining us and for their continued support of the people and organizations that strengthen community resilience."

"What makes Alpha Fire Company special is that service here creates opportunities that can change lives," said Brian Bittner, Fire Chief of Alpha Fire Company. "We have more than 100 volunteers, and close to one third are Penn State students who live and serve at the firehouse while pursuing their education. Many have been able to graduate while saving money and launching their careers, all while giving back to the community. Support from organizations like Bloom Energy helps us continue investing in our people, our equipment, and our mission to serve."
